Hi team — ops/infra here. I pulled the artifacts and drafted a short technical summary. Outline below and I attached samples to the shared folder.

Technical summary (high level):
- Processing region: All customer request routing for Acme will be pinned to Frankfurt (eu-central-1) and Amsterdam (eu-west-1) fleets via our smart routing policy; backup fallbacks are within EU regions only.
- Data partitioning: Customer data is logically segmented per-tenant and stored on EEA-only storage backends. Backups are replicated within EEA regions; cross-region replication outside EEA is disabled for this account.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. We use a customer-key-support model: by default Redwood-managed KMS keys (stored in EU KMS) unless customer elects a customer-managed key. Where Redwood-managed keys are used, we enforce strict RBAC and require an approval workflow for key deletion.
- KMS logs: attached is kms_access_report_20261101.csv (sample with principals and operations; IPs redacted per legal guidance).
- Human access: No routine human access to decrypted user content from outside the EEA. Emergency access (break-glass) is documented; approvals require two SRE leads and audit logging.
- Subprocessors: list included in redwood_eu_processing_dataflow.pdf. All subprocessors used for EU deployments maintain EU-hosted infrastructure.

Attachments placed in drive (view-only): redwood_eu_processing_dataflow.pdf, kms_access_report_20261101.csv, audit-log-samples-202610.zip. I also added a short playbook excerpt describing break-glass workflows and audit trail retention.

ETA: I can produce a one-page technical cover memo by Thursday (Nov 5) EOD. If Acme needs raw logs with full IPs we should require an NDA and a separate secure transfer.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Infra Ops, Redwood Inference
